title: Integrate runbook and probe signals into release curator
author: Asha Verma
description:
Context and motivation: Customers and internal users increasingly ask not just what changed in a model release but why it matters operationally. We observed multiple incidents and postmortems where a model profile delta or a change in performance telemetry (latency/timeout spikes, token-level OOMs) lacked a direct link in the release notes to runbooks, mitigations, or probe evidence. This PR augments the release curator with two signal classes: (1) runbook references surfaced from incident/runbook tags attached to model onboarding or variant updates, and (2) sampled probe telemetry anchors (aggregated metrics + representative diffs) so changelogs include concrete operational context.

Design summary: Add a runbook signal ingestion pipeline that consumes runbook metadata (id, severity, short description) attached to model-version and variant records; wire a lightweight sampler that collects jitter-resistant probe snippets (latency histograms, prefix failure rates, small sample prompts) and produces compact evidence tokens. The release contextualizer stitches these signals into the autogenerated blurb using severity-aware templates (notice, advisory, urgent) and includes a short "What to watch" section with instrumentation links.

What changed in this PR: 1) curator/signal_ingest.py: new ingestion adapter for runbook metadata and probe samples; 2) curator/contextualizer.py: template engine update to accept runbook/probe anchors and render severity buckets; 3) onboarding/hooks.py: small change to attach runbook reference when a model variant is promoted; 4) tools/backfill_runbook_annotations.py: backfill script to annotate recent 90 days of releases from incident ledger; 5) tests/{unit,integration}/: added unit tests for templating and an integration test that verifies backfill idempotence; 6) docs/registry/release-context.md: doc with sample changelog output and best practices for runbook tags.

Implementation notes: - Runbook IDs are treated as free-form strings but normalized for the changelog (EX-INC-412 -> EX-412) to keep blurbs concise. - Probe sampling is rate-limited and uses reservoir sampling over a 24h window to avoid noisy short-lived spikes contaminating release notes. - The templates are intentionally conservative: runbook references only surface as advisories if severity >= 3 or if probe anchors show a regression exceeding configured watermarks. - All new config defaults to off for hosted customers; enterprise/private tenants can opt-in via a feature flag in tenant metadata.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for template rendering edge cases and a synthetic integration job that runs the backfill script against a snapshot of the incident ledger. CI added a lightweight e2e (fast path) that runs against mocked probe samples. All checks are green on the final run.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind tenant opt-in. Initial rollout to internal staging and the Curation team for 2 weeks. Run the backfill script once during staging to produce annotated release previews, then opt in a small set of customer tenants. Monitor for noisy changelog spam and adjust reservoir parameters if necessary.

Backward compatibility and migration: Non-opted tenants see no changes. The backfill script is idempotent and safe to run multiple times; it writes only annotation metadata and will not mutate historical artifact blobs.

Docs and usage: docs/registry/release-context.md includes examples of generated blurbs, how to tag runbooks during onboard, and operational guidance for interpreting probe anchors. CLI helper added: "redwood-registry annotate-runbook --file <ledger> --dry-run".

Open questions / future work: - Consider integrating with the Optimize pipeline to automatically surface quantization/regression tradeoffs alongside runbook advisories. - Add more expressive probes (token-level skew, attention dropout) if customers ask for richer evidence. - UX: provide an optional digest email for tenant SREs when a release includes an "urgent" advisory.

Related work: references ENG-6421 (improve release contextualization), PM-293 (customer ask: clearer operational blurbs), SUP-1187 (support incident that motivated the change).

review_thread: Jonah Klein: Can we guarantee that the runbook IDs are stable across moves? If the incident gets re-numbered upstream we might have dangling refs. Reply: We normalize runbook IDs at ingestion and store a provenance pointer to the incident ledger; if upstream renumbers, provenance mapping wins and the blurb shows the canonical ID.

Priya Nair: Small nit on the template—please shorten the 'What to watch' copy when severity=3. Reply: Done; template now collapses long lists into a single sentence and provides a link to expanded instrumentation.

Ellen Park: CI flakey on integration test in the first run. Requested: add a timeout guard and retry for mocked ledger calls. Reply: Added retry with exponential backoff and reran tests; green now. Approved.
test_plan: Run unit tests locally: pytest tests/unit -k contextualizer
Staging run: enable feature flag for internal-staging tenant and run backfill with --dry-run, inspect generated markdown
Canary: opt-in two non-critical tenants and verify changelog output and absence of spam
release_notes: Adds optional runbook and probe anchor annotations to autogenerated release notes. Feature is tenant-gated and off by default. Includes a backfill tool to annotate recent releases.
impact_statement: Improves signal-to-noise in release notes by providing operational context tied to runbooks and sampled probe telemetry; helps SREs and customers quickly triage model releases.
notes_for_oncall: If tenants report unexpected churn in changelog volume, disable the feature flag and report sample id strings to the Curation team.
Backfill can be cancelled safely; it writes only annotation metadata and is idempotent.
